Landing page or multi-page website: choosing for advertising and SEO

Choose a format to match your business, advertising and SEO goals. We explain the differences, CMS and integrations, with costs from RESET projects.

A landing page suits a specific offer and a clear next step: check the terms, request a selection of properties or book a consultation. A multi-page website is useful when visitors need to choose between products, explore properties and return for new information. The choice depends on business objectives, traffic sources and plans for developing the company's online presence.

Page count describes the format but says little about development complexity. A landing page can include a CMS, a calculator and CRM integration. A small multi-page website may cost less than that landing page.

01

How a landing page differs from a multi-page website

A landing page is also a website. It is usually built around one offer or a set of closely related journeys. It introduces the product, explains the terms, provides evidence and offers a next step.

For example, an agency wants to test interest in new-build homes with instalment payments. Visitors arrive from an ad, explore the offer and terms, then request a selection. One well-prepared page may be enough.

A multi-page website organises several independent areas. An agency might have new builds, resale apartments, houses and commercial premises, each with its own pages, offers and paths to an enquiry.

A landing page can sit within a larger website. A dedicated campaign page can coexist with a shared catalogue, company pages and informational resources. The formats can complement each other.

A privacy policy, thank-you page or second language does not change the landing page's main purpose. The distinction becomes meaningful when the project needs an independent structure for choosing and exploring different offers.

02

When a landing page is enough

At RESET, a landing page is one way to test a marketing hypothesis with a limited development scope. We first define the offer, the audience and the action that would indicate interest.

For an estate agency, this could mean apartments in a particular neighbourhood, new builds with specific purchase terms or a property sales service for owners. These hypotheses involve different audiences and motivations. Separating their advertising messages and landing pages can be useful.

A good landing page provides enough information to make the next decision. The first screen explains the offer. Subsequent sections show terms, property or project examples, answers to important questions and a clear way to contact the company.

The sections depend on the task. Reviews, photographs, specifications, company information and a form are useful when they help visitors assess the offer. There is little point in adding sections solely because a familiar template includes them.

Testing also requires analytics events and an established process for handling enquiries. Form submission counts alone are insufficient: you need to know whether people could be reached and whether their needs matched the offer.

03

When you need a multi-page website

A multi-page structure helps when different business areas need their own explanations and offers. Buying an apartment, selling a house and renting commercial premises are difficult to explain equally well on one general page.

A regularly changing catalogue is another reason. Visitors need search, filters, property pages and a way to return to a particular listing. The team needs a convenient way to update prices, descriptions and availability.

Property count alone is not the dividing line. An agency might have 50 listings while using its site only to collect requests for a personalised selection. A landing page could still meet the initial objective.

If the company wants to display each property separately, develop search visibility for different categories and expand its catalogue, that structure should be planned from the start. It affects URLs, data management, navigation and future development.

04

What to choose for Google Ads, Facebook and Instagram

Advertising needs a close match between the ad and the destination page. Someone interested in an apartment in a particular neighbourhood should find a continuation of that offer after clicking.

A landing page makes it easier to focus attention on one area. A neighbourhood, development or property page within a larger website can serve the same purpose. Advertising traffic does not all have to go to the homepage.

Several products and audiences may need separate landing pages. Whether to combine them within one website depends on their content, shared property data and development plans.

We explore the relationship between search query, ad and website in our article on Google Ads for real estate. For social advertising, the offer, creative and enquiry quality are also essential, as discussed in our guide to property advertising on Facebook and Instagram.

05

Why SEO growth often needs several pages

Different searches can express different needs. Someone searching for a two-room apartment in a particular neighbourhood expects suitable listings. Someone researching instalment terms needs an explanation.

Separate pages can provide an appropriate answer to each. In real estate, these may be catalogue categories, neighbourhoods, developments, individual properties and useful articles.

The number of URLs is not an objective in itself. Every page needs content and a clear role. Empty selections and repetitive filter combinations gain no value simply from having a separate address.

Google's site organisation guidance stresses a logical structure that helps people and search engines understand relationships between pages. This does not guarantee indexing for every listing or a particular ranking.

A landing page can also attract organic traffic. Its scope depends on how many distinct needs one page can meaningfully address. When SEO becomes a separate business priority, the required structure usually expands.

Read more about choosing these pages in our article on SEO for property websites.

06

CMS and integrations do not determine the format

A CMS lets the team manage content. Even a single-page website may need one if staff regularly update projects, photographs or offer terms.

CRM integration is useful when enquiries, traffic sources and selected properties need to reach the sales team's working system. Both landing pages and large catalogues can require it.

Calculators, interactive site plans, customer accounts, multiple languages and database synchronisation add their own requirements. Assuming that “one page must cost less” is therefore unreliable.

The same applies to platform choice. A website builder or CMS should be assessed against requirements: URL and metadata management, speed, indexing, redirects, catalogue handling and integrations. Custom development can implement specific logic, but its quality depends on implementation and ongoing support.

07

A common mistake: requesting contact details before explaining the offer

RESET has worked in real estate since 2017. We have used pages built around quizzes or “leave your details to see the price” forms to test initial reactions quickly.

Today, we explicitly assess whether visitors have enough information to enquire. Buyers may need to see the location, floor plans, building specifications and payment terms first. A form cannot resolve unanswered questions by itself.

Even a developer with two or three properties may need a detailed website. Information depth and buyer journeys determine the scope. A short campaign landing page can still be a useful part of that project.

08

Landing page and website costs: RESET examples

Specific projects and agreed scopes make a more useful comparison. The development prices below are in US dollars. They are examples, rather than fixed rates for every project of that type.

ProjectDevelopment costWhat the example includes
NIVELLUX$600A renovation and construction company website with services, projects, estimate enquiries, and Russian and Spanish versions
SHEPIT HOUSE$1000A development website with interactive site-plan selection, an instalment calculator and buyer information
Estate CRM for DELMAR$2000A web system for enquiries, properties and selections, including workflow management and integrations

NIVELLUX needed a clear presentation of its services and experience. This example shows how a small website can be assessed through its content and enquiry journey.

SHEPIT HOUSE required additional tools to help buyers choose. The $1000 figure covers website development. Advertising and other work described in the wider case study are not included in that amount.

Estate CRM for DELMAR addresses internal agency processes. It connects enquiries, properties, selections and team oversight, illustrating how broad web development can be.

The cost of a similar new project depends on functionality, content readiness, languages, data sources and integration requirements. A company website with a CMS and administration panel also needs a defined scope first. A CRM price cannot automatically be applied to any corporate website.

09

How we choose the format and prepare an estimate

We start with the business: what it sells, to whom, where enquiries will come from and what should happen afterwards.

Then we describe user journeys. Should visitors simply request a selection, or compare properties themselves? Are separate advertising pages needed? Who updates the data? Which business areas will grow through search?

We then develop the structure and identify the necessary modules. The estimate distinguishes pages, content work, catalogue management, forms, analytics, language versions and integrations. The client can see what affects the cost and what could move to a later phase.

A landing page can be expanded into a larger website. If that is already the plan, the technology and content organisation should support it. A complete rebuild should not come as a surprise after the first campaign.

We discuss the budget in more detail in our article on website development costs in the AI era.

10

What to prepare before choosing a format

For an initial discussion, describe the offer, audience, advertising and SEO plans, number of properties or services, and enquiry handling process. Existing websites, materials and examples of what works or causes problems are also useful.

For testing a specific offer, we can consider a landing page. For a catalogue, several business areas and search growth, we can design a broader website structure. In both cases, the scope and cost are agreed before development begins.
